messages.subject: using plyr to make predictions
parts:
I am trying to fit a number of different models to a set of data sets
and then use those models to make predictions.

This is what I have so far:

library(plyr)

#create a test dataset
d <-data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3), y = c(1.1, 1.9, 3.1, -1.1,
-1.9, -3.1), group = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"))
new = data.frame(x = c(1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5), group = c("a",
"a", "a", "b", "b", "b"))

#define the model
model <- function(df) {
lm(y ~ x, data=df)
}

#apply the model to each group
models <- dlply(d, .(group), model)

#define the prediction
prediction <- function(fit) {
predict(fit, newdata = new[1])
}

#make a prediction
# this works but applies each model to the whole of the new dataset
pred <- laply(models, prediction)

My question is - how do I use plyr to predict from the first dataset
using the 1st model, the 2nd dataset with the 2nd model ... and so on
and then combine the results into a single prediction dataset

thanks

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: using plyr to make predictions
parts:
> My question is - how do I use plyr to predict from the first dataset
> using the 1st model, the 2nd dataset with the 2nd model ...  and so on
> and then combine the results into a single prediction dataset

You can do something like this:

d <- data.frame(

x = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3),
y = c(1.1, 1.9, 3.1, -1.1, -1.9, -3.1),
group = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"))

models <- dlply(d, "group", function(df) lm(y ~ x, data=df))
groups <- dlply(new, "group")

mdply(cbind(mod = models, df = groups), function(mod, df) {
transform(df, pred = predict(mod, df))
})


The key is the use of mdply to line up each group with the respective model.
